quote: In a world like that, all background knowledge is universal knowledge.
content: Barth's Baktaman withhold secrets; they do not build hundred-step arguments. Restricted ritual knowledge is private knowledge in the essay's sense. It is released by being told, and the initiate needs no chain of premises to follow the telling. Henrich's cumulative culture supports the essay's premise more than the note allows. His signature cases, such as the manioc processing that removes cyanide, are practices followed by people who cannot say why they work, so the knowledge lives in the practice and not in any argument that could be passed on (Henrich 2016, The Secret of Our Success, book, no DOI). A band whose deepest knowledge is embodied skill and unexplained custom is a world with no long explicit chains of inference, and so with no one who ever had to explain one.

quote: because it was a reliable invariant of the ancestral environment that this didn’t happen
content: The essay does not deny that people trust known, accurate informants selectively. Its scenario is someone who "says something with no obvious support," and there the vigilance literature is on the essay's side. People discount messages that clash with what they already believe unless the source has already earned their trust. That plausibility check is the first line of epistemic vigilance (Sperber et al. 2010; Mercier 2020, Not Born Yesterday, book, no DOI). An expert whose background the listener cannot see arrives as a stranger making an implausible claim and gets exactly the reception the essay predicts. The speaker's half of the story, the curse of knowledge, has its own experimental support in adults and in children (Camerer, Loewenstein & Weber 1989; Birch & Bloom 2007).

quote: the legendary difficulty most scientists have in communicating with a lay audience
content: The deficit model failed as a theory of attitude change on questions tied to identity. That is not the essay's subject, which is why explanations fail to be understood. Where an explanation lays out the inferential pathway, as the essay prescribes, it moves people: across several studies, a few hundred words on the mechanism of the greenhouse effect raised acceptance of global warming among liberals and conservatives alike (Ranney & Clark 2016). Kahan's polarization result concerns the best-informed members of groups that have already taken sides, whose disagreement is not about premises (Kahan et al. 2012). The essay's biologist is talking to someone who does not yet have the premises. The objection describes a different patient with a different disease.
